svg.title: Video watermarking
svg.desc: FFmpeg reads the video. CUDA tries NVDEC, OpenCL tries D3D11VA and QSV on Intel. Both hardware paths test the first frame before use, unsupported decoding uses CPU decode and GPU upload. Eigen stays on the CPU. Frames become 8-bit SDR before luma watermarking. Supported HDR uses GPU Mobius, other HDR uses CPU filters. Detection accepts only 8-bit SDR input, returns correlation results and stops. Embedding uses CPU encoding by default, optional hardware encoding uses NVENC, QSV or AMF on the same GPU. FFmpeg joins video with compatible audio and subtitle streams. A video batch runs one complete pipeline per selected GPU, each worker takes a whole file.

svg.text: Choose an encoder, keep the same backend and GPU

g.text: FFmpeg joins video, audio and subtitles

svg.text: CPU encoding is the default, --hw_encoder enables GPU encoding. SDR keeps 4:2:0, 4:2:2 or 4:4:4 when supported.
*GPU HDR supports limited-range BT.2020 PQ, 4:2:0, 10-bit input. Other HDR uses CPU filters.
CPU SDR converts before upload, skipped frames still get needed conversion, HDR tone mapping outputs 8-bit 4:2:0.
D3D11 frames use GPU copies and sharing for OpenCL. Watermarking changes luma (Y), the brightness plane.
A batch runs this full pipeline on each selected GPU, whole videos come from one shared queue.
